- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.

# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Healthcare
The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS expenditure by 2030, plus £20bn capital spending over five years for hospital building and repairs. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, ensuring NHS dentist availability for all, boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. Mental health services would receive investment to achieve parity with physical health, including counsellors in all schools. The party opposes NHS privatisation and supports the NHS Reinstatement Bill.

## Social Care
The manifesto proposes £20bn annual investment in social care, introducing free personal care (modelled on Scotland), establishing national pay and career structures for care workers, and improving support for disabled people including a 5% uplift to disability benefits.

## Housing
Plans include building 150,000 social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and investing £29bn over five years to insulate homes. Planning system reforms would protect green spaces while ensuring new developments include necessary infrastructure.

## Energy
The manifesto targets wind providing 70% of UK electricity by 2030, ending new oil and gas licences and fossil fuel subsidies, and introducing a carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne. Community ownership of energy infrastructure would be expanded, and nuclear power development would cease.

## Economy and Work
Proposals include £40bn average annual green investment, bringing railways, water companies, and major energy retailers into public ownership, establishing regional mutual banks, and increasing R&D investment by £30bn over five years. Worker protections would include a £15 minimum wage, maximum 10:1 pay ratios, repealing anti-union legislation, and movement toward a four-day week.

## Welfare
Universal Credit and legacy benefits would increase by £40 per week, the two-child benefit cap would be abolished, the bedroom tax scrapped, and carers' allowance increased by 10%.

## Taxation
The manifesto proposes a wealth tax (1% on assets above £10m, 2% above £1bn), aligning capital gains tax with income tax rates, and reforming inheritance tax. These measures are estimated to raise £50-70bn annually by parliament's end.

## Environment and Nature
A Rights of Nature Act would grant legal personhood to nature. The target is 30% of land and sea protected by 2030. Water companies would return to public ownership, with £1.5bn additional funding for environmental agencies.

## Education
Proposals include £8bn additional school funding, free school meals for all children, abolishing tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, and investing £5bn in SEND provision. Academies would return to local authority control.

## Transport
Annual public transport subsidies would reach £10bn, railways would be renationalised, and £2.5bn annually would fund cycling and walking infrastructure. Sales of new petrol and diesel vehicles would end by 2027.

## Democracy and Rights
Reforms include proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, and repealing voter ID requirements. The Human Rights Act and ECHR membership would be defended.

## Immigration
The manifesto proposes ending the hostile environment, establishing safe asylum routes, abolishing minimum income requirements for spousal visas, and allowing asylum seekers to work during application processing.

## Foreign Policy
Key positions include supporting an immediate Israel-Gaza ceasefire, recognising Palestine, ending UK arms exports to Israel, increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI, and working toward rejoining the EU. The party supports signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons while acknowledging NATO's defensive role.
